newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hang Lung unit signs HK$4.8 bln loan.
newsitem.headline: Hang Lung unit signs HK$4.8 bln loan.

text.p: Hang Lung Development Co Ltd is in its best financial shape in almost 20 years, a Hang Lung Development executive said on Monday.
Hang Lung Development Chairman Ronnie Chan said the company had not been so financially healthy for almost 20 years, and it had no plans to borrow in the second half of the year.
"Basically, our gearing ratio is almost zero, " he told Reuters at a signing ceremony for the company's HK$4.8 billion five-year term loan facility which is raised through a special purpose company.
Loan proceeds would be used to refinance debt, bankers told Reuters after the signing.
The blue-chip property company was able to push ahead a much lower funding cost than what it paid last year.
Hang Lung Development's interest bill would fall by HK$10 million to HK$20 million a year as a result of the loan, Chan said.
The loan carried a Hang Lung Development guarantee and paid an interest margin of 50 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.
Fees were 32.5 basis points for co-lead managers committing HK$150 Million, and 25 basis points for senior managers committing HK$75 million, bankers told Reuters.

Arrangers with HK$280 million each, are ABN Amro Bank, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Banque Nationale de Paris, Bayerische Landesbank, Commerz East Asia, Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank, Deutsche Bank, Fuji Bank, Sakura Bank, Societe Generale Asia, Sumitomo Bank, WestLB and BZW Asia, they said.
Co-lead managers with HK$150 million each, are Hamburgische Landesbank-Girozentrale Hong Kong, Industrial Bank of Japan, Mitsubishi Trust and Banking Corp and Tokai Bank.
Senior managers with HK$70 million each, are Bank of Communications Hong Kong, Development Bank of Singapore, Tokyo Trust and Banking Co and Wing Lung Bank.
